sources.title: Further Correspondence respecting the Affairs of Central Asia — Central Asia No. 2 (1887)
sources.institution: British Foreign Office / Her Majesty's Stationery Office
sources.coverage: British Parliamentary command paper containing the 1885-1887 Anglo-Russian Afghan boundary correspondence, protocols, maps and coordinate-bearing annexes
sources.notes: Presented to both Houses of Parliament by Command of Her Majesty in September 1887. The coordinate-bearing protocol annex defines trigonometric control points and explicitly distinguishes straight, watershed and thalweg segments.

sources.title: Russian official publication of the 1887 Anglo-Russian Afghan boundary protocol
sources.institution: Russian Empire official treaty/legal publication, digitized by Great Russian Encyclopedia
sources.coverage: Parallel Russian/French publication of the 1887 boundary protocol and its coordinate-bearing frontier description
sources.notes: Used to cross-check OCR-damaged coordinate values in the British parliamentary scan; the Russian text clearly prints 62°27′57″ for pillar 24, 35°18′21″ for Kalari 2, and 62°59′43″ for Tori-Sheikh.

sources.title: Protocols of the Commission instituted by the Protocol of July 22, 1887, for the Delimitation of the North-West Boundary of Afghanistan
sources.institution: United Kingdom Treaty Series, digital legal archive copy via BAILII
sources.coverage: Final Anglo-Russian commission protocols completing the north-west Afghan demarcation on 26 January 1888

sources.title: A Collection of Treaties, Engagements and Sanads relating to India and neighbouring countries, vol. XIII, Afghanistan Appendix I
sources.institution: Government of India / India Office; British Library IOR/L/PS/20/G3/14
sources.coverage: 1933 Government of India fifth edition reproducing the completed Description of the Afghan Frontier between the Hari Rud and the Oxus, including pillar-by-pillar route semantics
sources.notes: Revised in 1930 and published in Delhi in 1933 by the Manager of Publications under Government of India authority. Appendix I begins on printed p. 251 / QDL image 494 and provides the completed frontier description. It is used as an official retrospective compilation of the commission route, not as a substitute for the original signed maps where exact terrain tracing is required.

sources.title: Map illustrative of the Afghan Boundary Commission march and the frontier as proposed and actually demarcated
sources.institution: Library of Congress Geography and Map Division
sources.coverage: Contemporary contextual map showing the proposed and actually demarcated 1885-1888 north-west Afghan frontier
sources.notes: Useful contemporary cartographic context and Library of Congress catalog evidence for the commission route and completed frontier, but not treated as the canonical signed demarcation map and not used as evidence for geometry-verified fragments.
